back: The tag moves, so the deployment is not reproducible. Tag by immutable version. Keyword: pin the version.
A shared credential that should stay disabled; use Entra with AcrPull/AcrPush or a managed identity. Keyword: disable it.
Rebuilds every image built on a base when that base is patched — fleet-wide patching with nobody remembering. Keyword: automatic rebuild.
Immutable configuration snapshots with traffic splitting by percentage — blue-green as a config change. Keyword: split traffic.
Container Apps hides Kubernetes and scales to zero. AKS gives the primitives and the operational burden. Keyword: do you need the primitives.
A queue worker scales on queue depth, not CPU — CPU stays low while a backlog builds. Keyword: scale on the signal.
Cheap for intermittent workloads, at the cost of a cold start on the next request. Keyword: latency for cost.
Warm the new version then swap — near-instant and reversible. Keyword: swap, don't redeploy.
Mark a setting slot-specific so a connection string does not follow the swap. Keyword: stays behind.

front: Key Vault reference in app settings
back: Resolves at runtime through the managed identity, so the secret lives in one place and rotates without redeploying. Keyword: reference, not value.
Wrong tag, private registry with no credential, or a missing AcrPull role. Keyword: it never started.
The container starts and exits repeatedly — the cause is in the container's own logs, not the platform events. Keyword: read the app logs.
Create once and reuse; one per request exhausts connections and adds latency to every call. Keyword: reuse the client.
Returned on every Cosmos response — the direct measure of what a design costs. Keyword: measure, don't estimate.
Everything is indexed by default; excluding unused paths cuts the RU cost of every write. Keyword: exclude for writes.
Guarantees read-your-own-writes and is usually correct; strong raises RU cost and constrains availability. Keyword: don't over-specify.
Nothing errors when an embedding no longer matches its document — the system returns confident wrong results. Keyword: no error.
How the change feed processor distributes work; a real container needing its own throughput. Keyword: provision it.
Creates and updates only — a delete must be a soft-delete update for a consumer to see it. Keyword: soft delete.
Every similarity query scans every row — correct and unscalable. Keyword: build the index.
Its lists are derived from existing rows, so building on an empty table produces a useless index. Keyword: load then index.
HNSW gives better recall and query speed at higher build cost and memory. Keyword: pay to search faster.
Query-time knobs trading recall against latency for HNSW and IVFFlat respectively. Keyword: tune at query time.

front: Vector index not fitting in memory
back: It is read from disk on every query — the usual reason vector search is slow on adequate-looking hardware. Keyword: size the memory.
Restricting by tenant, type, or date alongside similarity is what makes retrieval useful rather than merely close. Keyword: filter and search.
A correctness bug that appears weeks later. Keyword: decide how it goes stale.
Caches model responses by meaning, so equivalent questions hit the same answer — and the similarity threshold is a correctness setting. Keyword: close is not the same.
A queue delivers each message to one consumer; a topic delivers a copy to each subscription. Keyword: one or many.
Peek-lock allows complete or abandon and redelivers on lock expiry. Receive-and-delete loses the message if the consumer fails. Keyword: at-least-once needs peek-lock.
Receives messages exceeding max delivery count or expiring, so poison messages do not block the queue. Keyword: monitor it.
Ordered, related message groups handled by one consumer at a time — per-entity ordering without serialising everything. Keyword: ordered per key.
Event Grid announces that something happened; Service Bus hands over work to be processed. Keyword: notify vs process.
By event type, subject prefix and suffix, or advanced payload filters — cheaper and simpler than filtering in code. Keyword: filter at source.
Undeliverable events go to a storage destination that must be configured, or they are lost. Keyword: configure it or lose them.
The trigger decides when it runs; input and output bindings connect to data without connection-handling code. Keyword: when vs what.
A change feed processor with the lease container managed for you — the usual way to react to document changes. Keyword: managed leases.
Consumption scales to zero with cold starts. Premium pre-warms instances and adds VNet integration. Keyword: cold start or not.
Add orchestration for stateful workflows — fan-out/fan-in, approvals, long sequences — which stateless functions cannot express. Keyword: state.
Decide which messages each subscriber receives, so one topic serves several consumers with different interests. Keyword: per subscription.

front: Key Vault RBAC over access policies
back: RBAC scopes to an individual secret and is managed like every other Azure permission. Keyword: per-secret scope.
Stops even a privileged user destroying a vault before retention expires. Soft delete alone does not. Keyword: cannot be purged.
A rotated secret then breaks the application — read it rather than holding it forever. Keyword: rotation breaks caches.
Separate environments so the same key resolves differently in dev and production. Keyword: one key, many values.

front: Key Vault reference from App Configuration
back: Lets an app read everything from one place while secrets stay in the vault. Keyword: one read path.
Carried in headers across service boundaries; a service that drops it breaks the trace exactly where it was most needed. Keyword: async boundaries drop it.
Reduces volume and cost, but aggressive sampling loses the rare slow request that motivated tracing. Keyword: don't sample away the outlier.
Filtering after aggregation aggregates data that is then discarded. Keyword: where before summarize.
A dependency failure names the downstream service and is usually more informative than the request failure it caused. Keyword: look downstream.
The container exceeded its memory limit — a limit or a leak, not a platform fault. Keyword: memory limit.
Logs, then events, then connectivity. Restarting the cluster first destroys the evidence. Keyword: read before restarting.
